analysis:
Compared the complete troubleshooting BASE/HEAD and examined the new recovery policy, added-file metadata and bounded ServingReadiness orientation excerpt. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md:83,143 adds authorization diagnostics and idle-only re-registration guidance; it does not instruct bypassing authorization or deleting credentials. UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift:23–35 requires an unauthorized interval and !busy, then applies capped exponential retry spacing. Lines 42–48 classify missing status, untrusted/offline status and expired non-legacy authorization for recovery; this helper neither grants permission nor handles plaintext, keys, billing or cache data. No independently supported regression is visible. Existing installation, privileged-helper, report-redaction and cache guidance is unchanged, including the T-041 kill switch.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (referenced at troubleshooting.md:143), connection lifecycle and authorization-state dependencies: ensure busy covers queued/accepted and local requests, loads, Autopilot, drains and updates; retry counters survive reconnects and jitter is actually applied; reconnect invalidates old connection-bound grants and stale status rather than extending proof lifetime (T-053, TB-011, A-016); and re-registration does not bypass native-call admission or coordinator recovery limits (T-057). The added ServingReadiness.swift metadata and short excerpt are insufficient to verify its full diagnostic/logging behavior, hold handling or identity exposure (T-058, T-059, A-018). Missing implementations are coverage limits, not evidence of missing controls. These material cross-file questions require integration review.
